translation:
This medicine also treats all yang-excess and yin-deficiency, wind-heat and dryness-depression, dizziness and dimness of the head and eyes, wind-stroke with hemiplegia (偏枯), accumulated toxins from excessive wine, all astringent, stagnant, and obstructed conditions of the intestines and stomach, sores, tinea, atrophy and bi (痿痹), and also cold damage and miscellaneous diseases, vexation and thirst, and [conditions where] qi and fluids cannot be diffused and freed; all are suitable to take it.

Ginseng (人參), Atractylodes (白朮), Dang Gui (當歸), peony (芍藥), rhubarb (大黃), Gardenia (山梔子), Alisma (澤瀉) (each of the above half liang); Forsythia (連翹), Trichosanthes root (栝蔞根), dried Pueraria (乾葛), Poria (茯苓) (each of the above one liang); cassia bark (官桂), costus root (木香), patchouli (藿香) (each one fen); mirabilite (寒水石), licorice (甘草) (each two liang); gypsum (石膏) (four liang); talc (滑石), niter (盆硝) (each half liang).

Grind the above into a coarse powder; take five qian each time, with one cup of water and three slices of fresh ginger, decoct together until half a cup, squeeze out the juice, add a little honey, and take warm. Gradually increase to more than ten qian, at no fixed time, three times daily.
translator_notes: 無時 rendered as 'at no fixed time'.
